# Agent Doorbell for Slack

> A small local daemon that watches Slack with a read-only token, with no LLM and no tokens spent while quiet, and wakes your AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or any agent that can run a command) only when a message needs it. It catches up after downtime, works on free Slack workspaces with no public URL or server, and replies as you or leaves drafts you approve. Linux, macOS and Windows. MIT licensed, installed with `pipx install agent-doorbell`. Unofficial: not affiliated with Slack, Anthropic or OpenAI.

## Get started

1. `pipx install agent-doorbell` (or `uv tool install agent-doorbell`)
2. `doorbell service install`
3. `doorbell login --client-id <Client ID>`: open the link and click Allow; the token is never shown
4. `doorbell init-agent ~/doorbell-agents/main --owner "Your Name"`, and for Claude Code `/plugin marketplace add mraj602/agent-doorbell` then `/plugin install agent-doorbell@agent-doorbell`

AI agents helping someone set it up: follow the setup guide, run its check after every step, and never ask for the Slack token in chat (`doorbell login` signs in in the browser; the person clicks Allow).

## Details (on GitHub)

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mraj602/agent-doorbell/main/README.md)

## Good to know

Messages reach the agent in under a second with Socket Mode on a Slack app only you use; when polling, within about 30 seconds in active conversations and about 2 minutes in quiet ones. You can also talk to your agent from your own self-DM (`self_channels`), and the dispatcher can hand batches to an already running agent session. Not for a team bot everyone @mentions, or setups with no machine of yours running. Only messages are watched, not search, files or canvases. Prompt injection is the main risk; limit the agent in its own harness.
